counterfactual_missing_items: negative staining for Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus
history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas does not match the current histopathology findings
decisive_items: concentric proliferation of ovoid tumor cells present around small vessels
CD31 immunostain highlighted many endothelial-lined vascular channels
Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was diffusely positive in the tumor cells
response.rationale: The champion candidate R3 is supported by multiple raw spans indicating a vascular origin of the tumor, including the presence of tumor cells around small vessels and positive CD31 and smooth muscle actin immunostains. The runner-up candidate C1 is a more specific version of R3, but it is not as strongly supported by the raw spans. The other candidates are contradicted by the raw spans or lack supporting evidence.

rejected.why: Negative staining for Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus contradicts the diagnosis of Kaposi sarcoma.
Histopathology findings do not support the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.
